question.problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{2}+1$ at the point $(2,9).$

$x\,+$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+1)=4x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,9):$

$$
m={f}^{′}(2)=4(2)=8
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-9 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-2) \\ 8y-72 & =-x+2 \\ x+8\cdot y & =74.\end{aligned}
$$
